page: Amazon Web Services c8i.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server featuring 384 vCPUs across 192 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores. Operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides dedicated CPU allocation with 480 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps but does not feature any local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier (top 10%) for multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation. It also achieves top-tier rankings in memory bandwidth, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 30,905.23 GB/sec and large block uncached speeds at 1,170.89 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations also rank in the top 10%, with Redis SET operations reaching 510.74 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench image processing scoring in the average tier (middle 50%).

The c8i.metal-96xl offers high compute density, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for highly parallelized, CPU-bound workloads that can leverage advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. Additionally, while prompt processing for large language models ranks in the top 25%, text generation speeds for small models fall into the bottom 10%, indicating that this CPU-only architecture is less suited for low-latency LLM text generation compared to GPU-accelerated alternatives.

This server is designed for highly parallelized workloads, including large-scale software compilation, multi-threaded data decompression, high-throughput web serving, and database operations. It also supports CPU-based scientific simulations and cryptographic processing.
